在 BD MAX 肠道病毒检测组确认的 185 份 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 阳性结果中,不同地点的错误发现率在 31% 至 74% 之间,其中在专门的癌症护理医院中发现的错误率最高。 [10.1128/jcm.00745-26]

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 经确认的 诺如病毒 暴发 数据显示,暴发 减少了 53%(2025-2026 年为 1,194 个,2024-2025 年为 2,534 个),CDC 描述为在 2012-2025 年季节性年份的典型范围内。 [news-8721243127156c4c]
在国家地理海鸟游轮上确认了诺如病毒 暴发。CDC 自 5 月下旬以来报告了第三个和第四个 暴发,前两个 暴发 已得到实验室确认。最近一次暴发发生在7月10日至15日和7月15日至20日的航程中。 [news-957ac1e2816f67e4]
国家地理海鸟号确认胃肠道疾病 暴发,这是该船在不到两个月的时间内第四次出现 暴发。症状:腹部绞痛、呕吐、腹泻。 [news-066090e7db2cce4e]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: Confirmed norovirus outbreak data showing a 53% decrease in outbreaks (1,194 in 2025-2026 vs. 2,534 in 2024-2025), described by CDC as within the typical range for seasonal years 2012-2025. [news-8721243127156c4c]

Confirmed norovirus outbreaks on the National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship. The CDC reported the third and fourth outbreaks since late May, with laboratory confirmation for the first two outbreaks. The most recent outbreaks occurred during July 10th–15th and July 15th–20th voyages. [news-957ac1e2816f67e4]

Confirmed gastrointestinal illness outbreak on National Geographic Sea Bird, marking the vessel's fourth outbreak in less than two months. Symptoms: abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea. [news-066090e7db2cce4e]

papers.title: Molecular characterization of norovirus false-positive results on the BioFire FilmArray gastrointestinal panel
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Molecular syndromic panels such as the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BF-GIP) have been widely adopted for gastrointestinal illness diagnosis due to their fast turnaround times and broad pathogen coverage. Recently, the BF-GIP demonstrated increased rates of norovirus false-positive detections, prompting a Class II recall of more than two million tests in February 2024 and resulting in an estimated burden of more than a quarter-million false-positive norovirus results reported over the last 5 years. We examined the prevalence of BF-GIP norovirus false positives across four hospitals from December 2024 to June 2025. Among 185 BF-GIP norovirus-positive results confirmed with the BD MAX Enteric Viral Panel, the false discovery rate ranged from 31% to 74% across sites, with the highest rate seen at a specialized cancer care hospital. Deep sequencing of BF-GIP pouches (n = 42) confirmed the Noro-1 assay as the primary source of off-target amplification, identifying 78 off-target species-predominantly commensal stool bacteria-compared to only two species for the Noro-2 assay. Off-target species amplified by the Noro-1 assay were recovered from both false-positive and true-negative pouches, suggesting no single species accounted for the false-positive results. Partial primer complementarity at off-target loci and amplicon Tm values within the acceptable range support mispriming of gut microbiota as the underlying cause. False-positive pouches exhibited significantly higher crossing point values than true-positive pouches for both assays (Noro-1: 26.6 vs 11.1, P = 0.013; Noro-2: 30.0 vs 13.1, P < 0.001), consistent with low-level off-target amplification. These findings highlight the high false discovery rate of the Noro-1 assay, identify bacterial species involved in mispriming, and demonstrate the need to redesign this assay to ensure reliable testing and improved patient care. IMPORTANCE: Syndromic molecular panels have revolutionized gastrointestinal diagnostics. However, recent data have suggested significant norovirus false-positive results associated with the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel. Here, we investigate a major diagnostic failure associated with the 2024 Class II recall of this assay, revealing norovirus false discovery rates as high as 74% in certain clinical settings. By deep sequencing amplicons from FilmArray pouches, we identified widespread cross-reactivity of the Noro-1 assay with stool microbiome nucleic acid. Off-target Noro-1 amplicons were detected from 78 bacterial species across 42 clinical pouches. For 16 species with the highest read counts per pouch, amplicons mapped to discrete genomic loci with partial primer overlap, consistent with mispriming. The identification of these discrete loci, combined with the repeatedly high false discovery rate reported across multiple studies, creates a clinical imperative to redesign this assay. Our work also highlights the ongoing need for rigorous post-market surveillance and the utility of deep sequencing in troubleshooting diagnostic assay failures.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the high false-positive rate of norovirus detection on the BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel (BF-GIP), which led to a Class II recall in 2024. Across four hospitals, the false discovery rate ranged from 31% to 74%, with the highest rate at a specialized cancer care hospital. Deep sequencing of BF-GIP pouches identified 78 bacterial species as off-target amplification sources, primarily from the Noro-1 assay. The findings confirm mispriming with gut microbiota as the cause, with partial primer complementarity and amplicon Tm values supporting this mechanism. The study underscores the need to redesign the Noro-1 assay and emphasizes the importance of post-market surveillance for molecular diagnostic panels.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: BioFire FilmArray Gastrointestinal Panel 等分子综合征组合由于周转时间短和病原体覆盖范围广而被广泛用于胃肠道疾病 诊断,但最近的数据表明与该组合相关的 诺如病毒 存在显着的假阳性结果。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们检查了 2024 年 12 月至 2025 年 6 月期间四家医院的 BF-GIP 诺如病毒 的 患病率 假阳性情况。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现凸显了 Noro-1 检测的高错误发现率,识别了引发错误的细菌种类,并证明需要重新设计该检测以确保可靠的检测和改善患者护理。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 具有部分引物重叠的离散基因座的识别,加上多项研究报告的反复高错误发现率,使得重新设计该检测方法成为临床上的当务之急,并强调了对严格的上市后 监测 的持续需求。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 具有部分引物重叠的离散基因座的识别,加上多项研究报告的反复高错误发现率,使得重新设计该检测方法成为临床上的当务之急,并强调了对严格的上市后 监测 的持续需求。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管该研究仅限于四家医院并且可能无法代表所有临床环境,但由于样本量大和验证性测试,证据强度很高。

papers.title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation Against Norovirus Infection: From Mechanisms to Clinical Evidence
papers.abstract: Norovirus (NoV) is a leading global cause of acute gastroenteritis. Infected individuals shed virus at high concentrations in feces, and an extremely low infectious dose enables secondary transmission among household contacts, thereby expanding the scope of spread. Currently, no approved specific antiviral therapies for NoV infection are available; therefore, it is urgent to develop novel therapeutic strategies. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) restores intestinal microbiota homeostasis by transplanting fecal microbiota from healthy donors, with well-proven efficacy in recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. This narrative review summarizes the biological characteristics and infection mechanisms of NoV, the bidirectional interplay between intestinal microbiota and NoV, and the clinical evidence supporting FMT application in NoV infection. This review also discusses the potential therapeutic mechanisms of FMT in NoV infection, including microbiota engraftment and structural remodeling, repair of the intestinal mucosal barrier, and immune modulation, and highlights key considerations for its clinical application, such as donor screening, fecal preparation and delivery routes. Existing evidence suggests that FMT may present favorable efficacy and safety in the management of NoV infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients. Nevertheless, current studies are limited to case reports and small case series, lacking large-scale randomized controlled trials. Further high-quality studies and standardized protocols are required to validate the clinical value of FMT and facilitate its clinical translation for the management of NoV infection.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on norovirus (NoV) as a leading global cause of acute gastroenteritis, examining its biological characteristics, infection mechanisms, and the potential of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as a therapeutic strategy. The central question is whether FMT can effectively treat NoV infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that summarizes existing evidence on NoV biology, microbiota-virus interactions, and clinical applications of FMT. The review does not specify databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria, nor does it report a meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The consensus is that FMT may present favorable efficacy and safety in managing NoV infection, especially in immunocompromised patients. Key conclusions include the potential therapeutic mechanisms of FMT, such as microbiota engraftment, mucosal barrier repair, and immune modulation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Current evidence is limited to case reports and small case series, lacking large-scale randomized controlled trials. There is a need for standardized protocols and high-quality studies to validate the clinical value of FMT for NoV infection.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further high-quality studies and standardized protocols are required to validate the clinical value of FMT and facilitate its clinical translation. Key considerations for clinical application include donor screening, fecal preparation, and delivery routes.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines norovirus (NoV) as a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis and explores fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) as a potential therapeutic strategy. The review summarizes NoV's biological characteristics, infection mechanisms, and the bidirectional interplay between intestinal microbiota and NoV. It highlights FMT's potential therapeutic mechanisms, including microbiota engraftment, mucosal barrier repair, and immune modulation. While existing evidence suggests FMT may be effective and safe, particularly in immunocompromised patients, current studies are limited to case reports and small series. The review emphasizes the need for larger randomized controlled trials and standardized protocols to validate FMT's clinical value and guide its implementation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 急性胃肠炎 的全球主要病因 诺如病毒 (NoV),研究其生物学特征、感染机制以及粪便微生物群移植 (FMT) 作为治疗策略的潜力。核心问题是 FMT 能否有效治疗 NoV 感染,尤其是免疫功能低下的患者。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,总结了 NoV 生物学、微生物群-病毒相互作用以及 FMT 临床应用的现有证据。该审查没有指定数据库、检索日期或资格标准,也没有报告荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 共识是,FMT 在治疗 NoV 感染方面可能具有良好的疗效和安全性,特别是对于免疫功能低下的患者。主要结论包括 FMT 的潜在治疗机制,例如微生物移植、粘膜屏障修复和免疫调节。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 目前的证据仅限于病例报告和小病例系列,缺乏大规模随机对照试验。需要标准化方案和高质量研究来验证 FMT 对 NoV 感染的临床价值。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步的高质量研究和标准化方案来验证 FMT 的临床价值并促进其临床转化。临床应用的关键考虑因素包括供体筛选、粪便准备和输送途径。

papers.title_zh: 粪便微生物群移植对抗 诺如病毒 感染:从机制到临床证据
papers.source_body_en: Norovirus (NoV) is a leading global cause of acute gastroenteritis. Infected individuals shed virus at high concentrations in feces, and an extremely low infectious dose enables secondary transmission among household contacts, thereby expanding the scope of spread. papers.abstract_zh: 诺如病毒 (NoV) 是 急性胃肠炎 的全球领先事业。感染者在粪便中排出高浓度病毒,极低的感染剂量可以在家庭接触者中继发传播,从而扩大传播范围。目前,尚无批准的针对 NoV 感染的 抗病毒药物 特效疗法;因此,迫切需要开发新的治疗策略。粪便微生物群移植(FMT)通过移植健康供体的粪便微生物群来恢复肠道微生物群稳态,对于复发性艰难梭菌感染的疗效已得到充分证明。本文总结了 NoV 的生物学特性和感染机制、肠道菌群与 NoV 之间的双向相互作用,以及支持 FMT 在 NoV 感染中应用的临床证据。本综述还讨论了 FMT 在 NoV 感染中的潜在治疗机制,包括微生物群植入和结构重塑、肠粘膜屏障修复和免疫调节,并强调了其临床应用的关键考虑因素,如供体筛选、粪便准备和输送途径。现有证据表明,FMT 在治疗 NoV 感染方面可能具有良好的疗效和安全性,特别是对于免疫功能低下的患者。然而,目前的研究仅限于病例报告和小病例系列,缺乏大规模的随机对照试验。需要进一步的高质量研究和标准化方案来验证 FMT 的临床价值并促进其在 NoV 感染管理中的临床转化。

papers.title: Efficient Production of Soluble Full-Length Norovirus VP1 in Escherichia coli ArcticExpress (DE3) with Potential for Diagnostic Assay Development.
papers.abstract: Abstract Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are one of the main causative agents of non-bacterial gastroenteritis. The viral capsid protein VP1 is the main target for diagnostics. Although eukaryotic expression systems can produce correctly assembled VP1, they are associated with high costs and complexity. The Escherichia coli prokaryotic expression system is attractive for large-scale expression; however, VP1 often aggregates into insoluble inclusion bodies in conventional strains (BL21 (DE3)). The ArcticExpress (DE3) strain co-expresses psychrophilic chaperonins to improve protein folding at low temperatures enhancing the soluble yield of difficult-to-express targets. In this study, we demonstrated that E. coli ArcticExpress (DE3) under low-temperature induction enabled the high-yield production of soluble full-length VP1 for HuNoVs GII.4 and GII.17. In BL21 (DE3), the mentioned antigens were aggregated into insoluble inclusion bodies. Using ArcticExpress(DE3), VP1 yield was identified as approximately 18–93 mg/L across the tested genotypes. In BL21 (DE3), the protein outcome was genotype-dependent: GII.4 could be recovered only via insoluble-fraction processing, GII.17 remained undetectable or present only at trace levels under the conditions tested. The ArcticExpress-derived viral antigen retained antigenic properties and was recognized by cross-reactive anti-GII antibodies. To our knowledge, this study provides evidence that ArcticExpress (DE3) enable the soluble production of full-length HuNoVs VP1 suitable for downstream immunochemical analysis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a major cause of non-bacterial gastroenteritis, and their capsid protein VP1 is a key diagnostic target. The study aimed to develop a cost-effective method for producing soluble full-length VP1 using a prokaryotic expression system.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized the Escherichia coli ArcticExpress (DE3) strain to produce soluble VP1 for HuNoVs GII.4 and GII.17 genotypes, comparing its performance with the conventional BL21 (DE3) strain.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed low-temperature induction in ArcticExpress (DE3) to enhance protein folding and soluble VP1 yield, followed by antigenic property validation using cross-reactive anti-GII antibodies.
analysis.main_results: ArcticExpress (DE3) produced soluble VP1 yields of 18–93 mg/L across tested genotypes, while BL21 (DE3) resulted in insoluble aggregates or undetectable levels. The ArcticExpress-derived VP1 retained antigenic properties.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that ArcticExpress (DE3) enables high-yield soluble production of full-length HuNoVs VP1, suitable for immunochemical analysis, addressing limitations of conventional expression systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method facilitates the development of diagnostic assays for norovirus by providing a scalable, cost-effective source of soluble VP1, improving surveillance and detection capabilities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is derived from a single study with limited genotypes, but the results are consistent and directly support the conclusions, indicating moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the challenge of producing soluble full-length norovirus VP1 protein for diagnostic purposes by using the Escherichia coli ArcticExpress (DE3) strain. The researchers demonstrated that low-temperature induction in ArcticExpress (DE3) yields high levels of soluble VP1 (18–93 mg/L) for HuNoVs GII.4 and GII.17, whereas the conventional BL21 (DE3) strain produced insoluble aggregates or undetectable protein. The ArcticExpress-derived VP1 retained antigenic properties, making it suitable for immunochemical analysis. This method offers a cost-effective alternative to eukaryotic systems, potentially advancing diagnostic assay development for norovirus gastroenteritis.

papers.title: IgA is necessary and sufficient to protect against norovirus infection 2258197
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Human norovirus (HNV) causes up to 700 million infections and 200,000 deaths each year, primarily affecting young children in low-resource settings. Despite this significant public health and economic impact, no licensed vaccines or anti-viral therapies exist for HNV. Several vaccine candidates are currently in advanced clinical trials, including virus-like particle (VLP), adenoviral (Ad5), and mRNA lipid nanoparticle (LNP) based vaccines. While these candidates show promise, none have demonstrated complete or long-term protection. The mechanisms underlying protective immunity to HNV remain poorly defined, posing a major barrier to rational vaccine design. Technical limitations make it challenging to directly interrogate mechanisms of HNV immunity, as there are no scalable cell culture, reverse genetics, or small animal models. Murine norovirus (MNV) is a genetically tractable model for HNV that shares many fundamental properties including minimal intestinal pathology, rare epithelial cell tropism, and fecal-oral transmission. Methods We used a panel of genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to investigate the correlates and cellular determinants of protection to MNV infection. Results T cell—dependent IgA is necessary to control MNV replication in the small intestine, whereas CD8+ T cells are dispensable. IgA plasma cells mediate protection from re-infection and dimeric IgA, but not monomeric, is sufficient to confer complete protection against MNV infection. In contrast, despite generating a robust systemic IgG response, systemic vaccination with the viral capsid protein (VP1) fails to protect mice, mirroring the recent failure of a systemic VLP vaccine in infants. Conclusion Our work shows that mucosal IgA is central to controlling norovirus infection in a murine model and provides important insights for rational vaccine design and HNV immunotherapeutics. Funding Source n/a Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis.study_design_and_population: We used a panel of genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to investigate the correlates and cellular determinants of protection to murine norovirus (MNV) infection, which serves as a genetically tractable model for HNV.
analysis.methods: We employed genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to investigate the correlates and cellular determinants of protection to MNV infection, focusing on T cell-dependent IgA and CD8+ T cells.
analysis.main_results: T cell-dependent IgA is necessary to control MNV replication in the small intestine, whereas CD8+ T cells are dispensable; IgA plasma cells mediate protection from re-infection, and dimeric IgA, but not monomeric, is sufficient to confer complete protection against MNV infection.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings highlight the critical role of mucosal IgA in norovirus protection, informing the development of effective vaccines and immunotherapeutics that target mucosal immunity rather than systemic responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a murine model, which may not fully recapitulate human norovirus infection; however, the evidence strength is high due to the rigorous use of genetically and pharmacologically modified mice to establish causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanisms of protective immunity against norovirus using a murine model. papers.title: Conformational Plasticity of the Human Norovirus GII.3 Capsid Reveals Alternative P Domain Interaction Networks
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, yet no effective antiviral therapeutics are currently available. Although environmentally induced capsid conformational changes associated with infectivity have been reported in murine noroviruses (MNVs), comparable conformational switching has not been demonstrated in HuNoVs. In this study, we generated HuNoV GII.3 virus-like particles (VLPs) using a baculovirus expression system and identified two distinct T = 3 particle populations coexisting within VLP preparations derived from a single strain through cryo-electron microscopy single-particle analysis. Comparative structural analysis revealed that these two T = 3 capsid conformations correspond to the resting and rising states of the protruding (P) domain. Rearrangement of the P domain alters intermolecular interactions between adjacent capsid subunits, resulting in distinct capsid surface architectures. In the resting state, intermolecular contacts were mediated predominantly by the P2 subdomain, with limited contribution from the P1 subdomain. In contrast, the rising state exhibited a shift toward an alternative interaction interface primarily involving the P1 subdomain. The alteration of the capsid surface accompanying this conformational switching can influence biologically relevant intermolecular interactions with viral hosts and antibodies as demonstrated in murine norovirus. These findings demonstrate previously unrecognized structural polymorphism in the HuNoV capsid and provide evidence that conformational switching may occur in HuNoVs. Our results offer new insights into norovirus capsid dynamics and may inform future structure-based vaccine and antiviral drug development.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoV) 是全球 急性胃肠炎 的主要原因,但目前尚无有效的 抗病毒药物 治疗方法。尽管在小鼠 诺如病毒 (MNV) 中已经报道了环境诱导的与感染性相关的衣壳构象变化,但在 HuNoV 中尚未证实类似的构象转换。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这项研究中,我们使用杆状病毒表达系统生成了 HuNoV GII.3 病毒样颗粒 (VLP),并通过冷冻电子显微镜单颗粒分析鉴定了在源自单一菌株的 VLP 制品中共存的两个不同的 T = 3 颗粒群。
elements_zh.methods: 比较结构分析表明,这两种 T = 3 衣壳构象对应于突出 (P) 结构域的静止和上升状态。P 结构域的重排改变了相邻衣壳亚基之间的分子间相互作用,导致不同的衣壳表面结构。
elements_zh.main_results: 在静息状态下,分子间接触主要由 P2 亚结构域介导,P1 亚结构域的贡献有限。相比之下,上升态表现出向主要涉及 P1 子域的替代相互作用界面的转变。伴随这种构象转换的衣壳表面的改变可以影响与病毒 宿主 和抗体的生物学相关的分子间相互作用,如小鼠 诺如病毒 中所证明的。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现证明了 HuNoV 衣壳中以前未被识别的结构多态性,并提供了 HuNoV 中可能发生构象转换的证据。我们的结果为 诺如病毒 衣壳动力学提供了新的见解,并可能为未来基于结构的 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 药物开发提供信息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,HuNoV 衣壳中的构象转换可能影响病毒 宿主 和抗体的相互作用,可能为基于结构的 疫苗 和 抗病毒药物 药物的开发提供信息。这种结构多态性可能对理解 诺如病毒 感染性和免疫逃避机制具有影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是使用病毒样颗粒而不是传染性病毒粒子进行的,这可能无法完全代表病毒的自然状态。然而,冷冻电子显微镜单颗粒分析的使用提供了高分辨率的结构数据,支持对证据强度的适度评估。

papers.title: Optimized MT-Capture targeted enrichment sequencing for the complete genome of norovirus in stool and sewage samples
papers.abstract: Human norovirus is a major acute gastroenteritis pathogen with high genotypic diversity, mutation, and recombination rates. Existing sequencing methods for monitoring its genetic variations are limited by low sensitivity and contamination risk. This study optimized our previously established Micro Target Hybrid Capture System (MT-Capture) by increasing nucleic acid input, streamlining library preparation, and introducing a deployable USER enzyme-based contamination prevention system. The optimized protocol completes library preparation and capture within 7 hours. Compared with multiplex PCR sequencing, optimized MT-Capture avoids primer updates, captures multiple genotypes with improved compatibility, and detects low-abundance samples more efficiently. The USER enzyme degrades contaminating amplicons, ensuring data authenticity. The MT-Capture-USER system provides a rapid, sensitive, and contamination-resistant approach for norovirus whole-genome sequencing and epidemiological surveillance.

papers.title: Individual-level factors associated with acute hospitalization after medically attended acute gastroenteritis and norovirus gastroenteritis in the United States, 2022–2024
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) in the United States and is associated with substantial healthcare utilization, including risk of hospitalization. The extent to which underlying medical conditions contribute to this risk is not well understood. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed adults with incident medically attended all-cause AGE or cause-specified norovirus AGE episodes identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2024 in Optum’s de-identified Clinformatics® Data Mart Database (Optum® CDM). Generalized estimating equations estimated adjusted risk ratios (aRRs) and confidence intervals (CIs) for acute hospitalization within three days of AGE diagnoses. Results Of 1,705,514 all-cause AGE and 5,805 norovirus AGE cases, 11.3% and 44.6%, respectively, were hospitalized within three days of their episode. Hospitalization risk was higher for patients with cardiovascular disease (all-cause AGE aRR: 1.67 [95% CI, 1.64–1.69]; norovirus AGE aRR: 1.37 [1.22–1.54]), blood disorders, chronic respiratory disease, and chronic kidney disease. analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated individual-level factors associated with acute hospitalization after medically attended acute gastroenteritis (AGE) and norovirus gastroenteritis in the United States from 2022 to 2024. Analyzing over 1.7 million all-cause AGE and 5,805 norovirus AGE cases, the study found that 11.3% and 44.6% of patients, respectively, were hospitalized within three days. Underlying conditions, particularly cardiovascular disease and the presence of two or more conditions, significantly increased hospitalization risk, with adjusted risk ratios ranging from 1.37 to 2.02. Notably, the relative risk was higher among adults aged 18–64 years compared to those 65 and older. These findings underscore the importance of considering comorbidities in assessing norovirus-related hospitalization risk, potentially guiding targeted clinical interventions and public health strategies.

papers.title: Regional and national burden and etiological patterns of diarrheal disease in Asia with implications for travel medicine
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the considerable burden of diarrheal disease in Asia, etiology-specific patterns remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive assessment of the diarrheal disease burden across Asia from 1990 to 2023, focusing on the implications for travelers' diarrhea. METHODS: We estimated the burden of diarrheal disease in Asia, including Central, East, South, Southeast Asia, and High-income Asia Pacific, across 34 countries from 1990 to 2023 using the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2023. Disease burden was calculated using age-standardized disability-adjusted life year rates (ASDRs) per 100,000 population, with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Additionally, we assessed the burden attributable to risk factors and calculated pathogen-specific estimates for 13 major etiologies. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, ASDRs of diarrheal disease declined across Asia, with the largest decline in South Asia from 9124.29 (95% UI, 7594.46-11,673.82) per 100,000 population to 1216.90 (965.73-1633.55). The decline was accompanied by reductions in cumulative etiologic burden, particularly for rotavirus. Although norovirus was the leading etiology in High-income Asia Pacific, rotavirus remained dominant across all other Asian regions in 2023. Burdens were concentrated among those aged <5 years and ≥95 years. Among children aged <5 years, rotavirus and adenovirus were the leading etiologies, with adenovirus showing a particularly high age-specific DALY rate in South Asia (891.96 [484.65-1392.81] per 100,000 population). Among adults aged ≥ 95years, Clostridium difficile and norovirus had the highest burdens. Sex-specific burdens were generally higher in males, except in South Asia. In 2023, unsafe water sources were the leading risk factor, especially in South Asia, 831.77 (423.32-1206.25) per 100,000 population. For viral, parasitic, and gram-negative etiologies, burdens consistently declined with increasing SDI, whereas Clostridium difficile showed a U-shaped pattern with SDI. CONCLUSIONS: The heterogeneity in etiology-specific burden, age- and sex-related vulnerability, and associations with SDI across Asia underscores the need for destination-specific risk assessment and context-sensitive prevention strategies for travelers' diarrhea in Asia.

papers.title: A 3-year wastewater-based epidemiology study of noroviruses in Senegal
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide due to its high contagiousness, widespread transmission, and the lack of treatment or vaccine. In Senegal, no routine community-level monitoring is performed, and most available data concern other enteric viruses, leaving a gap in understanding norovirus circulation. To assess the potential of wastewater surveillance as an early warning system, we analyzed the spatiotemporal circulation in Senegal of noroviruses using clinical and environmental data collected between 2020 and 2023, combining statistical and machine learning models, and comparing effective reproduction number R(t) estimates between genotypes and surveillance systems. Our data show that norovirus GII was the dominant genotype during the study period. In addition, a strong spatial heterogeneity in viral load was identified between wastewater collection sites, with high titers observed in several wastewater collection sites. Interestingly, peaks of viral load in environmental setting frequently preceded increases in reported clinical cases. Modeling data indicated more persistent circulation of norovirus GII than GI. Our findings also highlighted the influence of temporal, demographic, and clinical factors for viral loads in wastewater. Comparison of the effective reproduction number R(t) confirmed the descriptive data and highlighted a more persistent circulation for norovirus GII and a detection of R(t)'s increases in wastewater data prior to variation in clinical data, underscoring the usefulness of wastewater environmental surveillance as an early warning tool system for norovirus surveillance. Our study is noteworthy by representing the first countrywide application of wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor norovirus circulation across diverse geographic and demographic settings in Senegal. IMPORTANCE: Noroviruses represent a major public health concern worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, such as Senegal where resources are limited. Monitoring noroviruses in wastewater is critical for early detection of outbreaks and tracking viral evolution, as these viruses are often underdiagnosed in clinical settings. In this study, we report on the spatiotemporal circulation of noroviruses in Senegal using clinical and environmental data collected over 4 years and combining modeling methods with estimation of epidemiological parameters. Our study provides the first countrywide data on the application of wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor noroviruses across diverse geographic and demographic settings in Senegal. Our data offer a proactive, cost-effective method to monitor public health trends and identify the presence of noroviruses within the population, offering an early warning system for community spread. The approach could be useful for the monitoring of other public health concerns in Senegal in the absence of routine clinical surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a 3-year wastewater-based epidemiology investigation of noroviruses in Senegal, aiming to evaluate the potential of wastewater surveillance as an early warning system. The research combined clinical and environmental data from 2020 to 2023, using statistical and machine learning models to compare effective reproduction numbers (R(t)) between genotypes and surveillance systems. The main results showed that norovirus GII was the dominant genotype, with peaks in viral load in the environmental setting often preceding increases in clinical cases. The authors interpreted these findings as evidence of the utility of wastewater surveillance for tracking norovirus circulation and detecting outbreaks before they are clinically apparent. The study highlights the importance of wastewater-based methods for monitoring noroviruses, especially in low-resource settings where clinical surveillance is limited. However, the authors noted strong spatial heterogeneity in viral load across collection sites, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The study is significant for its countrywide application of wastewater-based epidemiology to monitor norovirus across diverse geographic and demographic settings in Senegal, offering a cost-effective early warning system for community spread. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the limitations in spatial uniformity and the potential for confounding factors.

papers.title: Pathogen Forecast Model Version 1.0: A Process-based Five-Day Beach Advisory Forecast System for the San Diego/Tijuana Region.
papers.abstract: The San Diego/Tijuana (US/Mexico) coastal region has immense water quality issues due to untreated wastewater sources. Regular ddPCR Enterococcus sampling provides same-day water quality information for beachgoers but does not provide forecasts for decision making. We describe the Pathogen Forecast Model (PFM) V1.0, providing daily 5 day forecasts of swimmer illness risk along 30 km of shoreline on a web dashboard. PFM is based upon a hydrodynamic model using forecasted waves, winds, offshore currents, and Tijuana River flow as inputs. PFM accurately forecasts tides and waves and forecasts depth-averaged shelf currents moderately well. Modeled untreated wastewater concentration tracer C evolves with a constant decay rate representing Norovirus. Over 13 km of shoreline, forecasted C and observed Enterococcus E are moderately log-correlated (≈0.5) for day-1 and -5 forecasts. The C and E power-law relationship has an exponent of ≈0.5, possibly suggesting the tracer decays 2× slower than Enterococcus DNA, among other potential explanations. papers.title: How Does Food Become Contaminated?
papers.abstract: The recognised foodborne hepatitis E strains are zoonotic and originate from infected animals. Therefore, they mainly contaminate foods intrinsically. Norovirus and hepatitis A virus, on the other hand, have their sources in infected humans and contaminate food extrinsically. Foodstuffs at risk of extrinsic contamination include fresh produce and shellfish and can be contaminated during primary production by contact with sewage-impacted waters. Foods can also be contaminated during all other phases of food supply (processing, retail, catering) by contact with infected food workers who do not employ proper hygienic practices. Outbreak features can illustrate the specific circumstances surrounding virus food contamination.

Conditions Norovirus Outbreaks Fell by More Than Half This Season, and CDC Says the Current Total Is Typical Published Jul 28, 2026 11:00 AM EDT By Cole Mercer HENNING KAISER/DDP | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Last winter's norovirus season was ugly enough that it produced a year of headlines about a stomach bug tearing through cruise ships, nursing homes and school cafeterias. This season, the same surveillance system counted fewer than half as many outbreaks.Between August 1, 2025 and May 7, 2026, state health departments participating in CDC's NoroSTAT network reported 1,194 norovirus outbreaks. In the same window a year earlier, those states reported 2,534.The more useful sentence is CDC's own framing of what that means. The agency says the 2025-2026 total sits "within the middle 50% of outbreaks (interquartile range)" reported in the same period across the 2012 through 2025 seasonal years.In other words, this is not a good season. It is an ordinary one. The season that felt catastrophic was the abnormal data point, and reading this year's decline as improvement gets the baseline backwards.What NoroSTAT Actually CountsThe number is easy to misread in two directions, so the method matters.NoroSTAT is a sentinel network, not a national census. Fourteen state health departments report through it: Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia and Wisconsin. Those states are not the country, and the composition changes. New Hampshire appears in the current season's list where Alabama appeared previously, which means year-over-year comparisons carry a small caveat built in.It counts outbreaks, not cases. CDC defines a norovirus outbreak as two or more similar illnesses from a common exposure, suspected or laboratory-confirmed. One outbreak in a nursing home can involve dozens of people. One outbreak at a wedding can involve two.It counts reported outbreaks, which is a function of whether someone investigated. An outbreak in a facility with an infection preventionist gets reported. The same cluster among a group of friends does not.Nationally, CDC estimates roughly 2,500 reported norovirus outbreaks a year and about 19 to 21 million illnesses, 109,000 hospitalizations and 900 deaths annually. Those national figures dwarf the sentinel count and are the right scale for understanding the burden.Reporting also lags. Participating states have seven business days to report; data are updated monthly, and the seasonal year runs through July 31. The figures here run through early May, so the season is not formally closed.Why Last Season Was the OutlierThe 2024-2025 season stood above the range CDC had recorded across more than a decade, and the explanation researchers offered at the time was a strain change rather than a change in the virus's severity.A genotype called GII.17 displaced the long-dominant strain, rising from a small share of outbreaks to roughly three-quarters of them. Jan Vinjé, who heads CDC's CaliciNet laboratory network, said at the time that it was too early to know whether the strain caused more severe illness and that "likely lower population immunity is the reason for the early surge."That is the standard mechanism. When a new genotype becomes dominant, the accumulated immunity in a population no longer matches the circulating virus well, more people are susceptible, and outbreak counts rise. As immunity catches up over a season or two, counts typically settle back toward the historical range, which is what the current data appear to show.This also means the decline is not evidence that anything was done differently. It is largely a consequence of a population that has now met GII.17.What This Changes for HouseholdsPractically, very little, and that is worth saying plainly rather than dressing the number up as good news.Norovirus remains the leading cause of vomiting, diarrhea and foodborne illness in the United States. Most outbreaks occur in long-term care facilities, followed by restaurants, schools, child care centers and occasionally cruise ships. A typical season still produces thousands of outbreaks nationally.The prevention advice does not change with the outbreak count, and one piece of it is regularly gotten wrong. Alcohol-based hand sanitizer is not reliably effective against norovirus. Handwashing with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds is what works, particularly after using the bathroom and before preparing food.The virus is unusually durable on surfaces and resistant to many common disinfectants. Cleaning after a vomiting or diarrhea incident calls for a bleach-based product or an EPA-registered disinfectant labeled effective against norovirus, and contaminated laundry should be handled with gloves and washed on the longest hot cycle.People are contagious from the onset of symptoms and for at least two days after recovery, and often longer. That is why food handlers should not return to work immediately after feeling better, and why anyone caring for a person in a household should keep washing hands well past the point the vomiting stops.Dehydration is the real danger, and it falls hardest on young children, adults over 65, and people who are immunocompromised. Signs that warrant medical attention include little or no urination, dizziness on standing, dry mouth and throat, unusual sleepiness or confusion, and in children, a lack of tears when crying.What Happens NextThe seasonal year closes July 31, and CDC updates NoroSTAT monthly, so a full-season figure should follow. CaliciNet publishes the circulating genotype distribution separately, and whether GII.17 remains dominant or another genotype starts gaining share is the variable most likely to determine what next winter looks like.Wastewater surveillance now provides an earlier signal than outbreak reports do, and it tends to move weeks ahead of the outbreak count.The confirmed finding is that sentinel-state outbreak reports fell from 2,534 to 1,194 year over year and now sit inside the normal historical range. The people most affected by norovirus remain residents of long-term care facilities and the very young and very old. The most useful action is soap and water rather than sanitizer. The central uncertainty is which genotype dominates next season. NoroSTAT states reported 1,194 outbreaks between August 1, 2025 and May 7, 2026, compared with 2,534 in the same period a year earlier.Is that a good sign? It is a normal one. CDC says the current total falls within the middle 50 percent of outbreaks reported over the 2012 through 2025 seasons. Last season was unusually high.Is this a national count? No. NoroSTAT is a 14-state sentinel network. CDC separately estimates roughly 2,500 reported norovirus outbreaks nationally each year.Why was last season so bad? A genotype called GII.17 became dominant, and lower population immunity to that strain was the leading explanation offered by CDC researchers.Does hand sanitizer work against norovirus? Not reliably. Wash hands with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds.How long am I contagious? From the start of symptoms until at least two days after recovery, and sometimes longer. Food handlers should not return to work as soon as they feel better.When should I seek care? news.content_title: Lindblad's National Geographic Sea Bird reported 4th Norovirus outbreak in Alaska
news.content: National Geographic Sea Bird , operated by Lindblad Expeditions , has experienced gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on two consecutive Southeast Alaskan voyages this month, with nearly 1/3rd of those on board affected during one of the sailings. According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the incidents represent the third and fourth reported outbreaks aboard the vessel since late May. The ship most recently called at Juneau on July 15th. The first of the two recent outbreaks occurred during the July 10th–15th voyage, when 19 of the 88 passengers and crew members on board became ill. The affected group included 18 passengers and one crew member. Reported symptoms included vomiting and abdominal cramps. During the subsequent July 15th–20th voyage, 13 of the 83 passengers and crew members were reported ill, comprising 8 passengers and 5 crew members. Those affected experienced diarrhoea, vomiting and abdominal cramps. In total, 32 passengers and crew members were affected across the two voyages. The CDC has not yet identified the cause of the latest outbreaks. However, laboratory testing previously confirmed norovirus as the cause of the vessel's first two outbreaks, which occurred in late May and late June. So far during the 2026 cruise season, the CDC has recorded 9 GI illness outbreaks on cruise ships, with 4 of those involving the Nat Geo Sea Bird. The vessel had been scheduled to return to Juneau on Saturday, July 25th, but according to Cruise Line Agencies of Alaska, that call has been cancelled. For more National Geographic Sea Bird incidents and accidents, see the ship's CruiseMinus page

news.content_title: 13 people sick in fourth cruise ship GI outbreak in less than 2 months
news.content: More than a dozen people got sick with gastrointestinal illness on a National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions cruise, marking the vessel's fourth outbreak in less than two months. Eight of the 57 guests sailing aboard National Geographic Sea Bird reported being ill during its July 15 voyage, along with five crew members, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Their main symptoms were abdominal cramps, vomiting and diarrhea. The cause is unknown. The ship is currently operating in Alaska, according to CruiseMapper . The cruise company implemented heightened disinfection and cleaning measures and isolated sick guests and employees, among other steps, according to the health agency. Lindblad told USA TODAY in an emailed statement that it canceled three voyages scheduled to embark on July 20, July 25 and July 30 "to conduct enhanced sanitation protocols aligned with the highest industry standards and provide additional time to help prevent the risk of further cases." "We are working directly with affected guests to provide refunds, support and alternative travel arrangements," the company added. The cases follow three other outbreaks on the ship since late May. The first two were caused by norovirus, while the cause of the third remains unknown, the CDC said. From ports decorated with centuries-old architecture to sunlit turquoise bays, a new eye-tracking study revealed the world's most beautiful cruise ports, with three Caribbean spots making the top 20. The research, conducted by travel insurance experts at AllClear, used eye-tracking technology to measure which of the world's travel hotspots are the most impressive to arrive at by sea. They measured which cruise ports caught people's attention first, and held it the longest, revealing the world's most captivating coastal arrivals. 1. Valletta Cruise Port, Malta A UNESCO World Heritage Site, our study's most beautiful cruise port is a masterpiece in harbour aesthetics. Its combination of golden limestone reflecting off the glistening water provides the ultimate, jaw-dropping arrival into this exciting Mediterranean city, and with the longest fixation time of any port in the study, Malta certainly earned its place as our number one. What cruisers will love: Walk into the historic town in just 15 minutes and explore St. John's Co-Cathedral with its Baroque artwork, or head to the Upper Barrakka Gardens for panoramic views of the harbour itself. 2. Port of Ushuaia, Argentina The starting point for any adventurous cruiser who wants to sail through the nerve-wracking Drake's Passage to reach Antarctica, the port of Ushuaia is nestled among the snow-capped Andes and is nothing short of gorgeous to sail in and out of. What cruisers will love: If you have some time in Ushuaia before you leave for Antarctica, you can ride the "End of the World Train", a heritage railway which shows off the scenic Tierra del Fuego National Park. 6. Aruba Cruise Terminal, Aruba Aruba Cruise Terminal is another beautiful port where you don't disembark miles away from excursions, with passengers just a short walk away from the city center. The cruise port itself showcases the capital's Dutch colonial architecture, which is incredibly colorful and, when set against the bright blue waters, looks breathtaking. What cruisers will love: Palm and Eagle beaches in Aruba are some of the most famous in the world. They're home to some of the softest sand and seawater so salty you can float with ease. If you're feeling more energetic, you can venture to Arikok National Park to hike, snorkel at the Antilla shipwreck, or take a boat to Renaissance Island, where you'll find free-roaming flamingos. 8. Overseas Passenger Terminal, Australia Sydney cruise terminal, known as the Overseas Passenger Terminal, is possibly one of the world's most iconic, with views of the world-famous Sydney Opera House and Harbour Bridge on both sides as you enter the port. The second you step off the boat, you're in the heart of the city, ready to explore all it has to offer. What cruisers will love: If you can't get enough of the views over the harbour, you can climb the Harbour Bridge itself. If you want to explore more of the coastline, you can walk from Manly to Coogee, or you can head further into the city to visit the Royal Botanic Garden, Taronga Zoo, or the Museum of Contemporary Art. Cruise ship medical facilities: What happens if you get sick or injured (or bitten by a monkey) The health agency previously told USA TODAY in an email that more than 90% of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruises with a confirmed cause are due to norovirus. "People joining the cruise ship may bring the virus to other passengers and crew," the CDC said. "Characteristics of norovirus that facilitate outbreaks include a low infective dose, easy person-to-person transmissibility, prolonged viral shedding, absence of long-term immunity, the ability of the virus to survive routine cleaning procedures, and the absence of a vaccine." The CDC has logged nine outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification so far in 2026. Norovirus was listed as the cause of five, and two were caused by E. coli. Twenty-three outbreaks met that threshold last year, with 18 caused by norovirus. Norovirus also was behind 15 out of 18 outbreaks in 2024. While the illness is often associated with cruise ships, those account for just 1% of reported outbreaks . Outbreaks are "often taking place within the community, and oftentimes we don't know that they're happening," Sarah R. Michaels, an assistant professor at Tulane University's Celia Scott Weatherhead School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, previously told USA TODAY . "Really, when we have these areas where people ... are in really close contact, things like day care facilities, nursing homes and cruise ships, it's more likely (to be) diagnosed, reported and brought to our attention." This story was updated to add new information. Nathan Diller is a consumer travel reporter for USA TODAY based in Nashville. You can reach him at ndiller@usatoday.com.
